title: Preparing the record phase
statement: Let $k,n\in\mathbb{N}$, let $x$ be a finite binary input, let $c$ be a configuration of a $k$-tape machine with states indexed by $\{0,\ldots,n\}$, let $a$ be an action, and choose a state index $q$, a binary table, an optional summary bit, an integer position $p$, and an output prefix. The round machine runs from a state-tail configuration whose summary tape stores the unary encoding of $q$ at position $q+2$ and whose table head is at $p$, to the record-phase initial configuration with the same table and summary but with the summary tape empty and its head at $0$. The run takes $3q+16$ steps and satisfies the round-span property.
hypotheses_covered: Natural numbers $k,n$ and finite binary input $x$
